sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Commercial Code, Civil Code, and Monetary and Financial Code, with EU Directives transposed into national legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-US Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (effective provisions on business profits and VIE/technology royalties)
France-China DTAA of 30 May 1984, as amended by the 2013 Protocol
France-Singapore DTAA of 9 September 1974, as amended
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI), ratified by France, applicable to the covered tax agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Sapin II) as amended; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th AMLD); Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, 'RBE'); Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-51 and R. 561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier; Article L. 561-2-2 C. mon. fin. (UBO definition and 25% threshold); TRACFIN (French FIU) guidance and jurisprudence of the Cour de cassation; Court of Justice of the European Union, Case C-37/20 (restriction of public access to UBO registers).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited copy of the incorporation power of attorney (pouvoir) executed by each shareholder for the constitution of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular officer in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the signatory state is party to the HCCH 1961 Convention) OR Consular Legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the UBO natural person's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority, certified notary public, or consular authority of the UBO's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / certificate of good standing (extrait de registre) for any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the foreign jurisdiction in which the corporate shareholder is incorporated

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate confirming the availability and deposit of share capital (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution acting as depositary bank for the share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal French financial document - no Apostille or consular legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence (CDD) under Article L. 561-5 of the Code monétaire et financier: screening of all UBOs, directors, and the corporate chain against (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and national implementing decrees), (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list, (iii) the OFAC SDN List (required as a practical condition for Stripe Billing and Wise B2B payment rails), (iv) the French Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor) embargo and asset-freeze lists, and (v) internal PEP and negative-media registers referencing the FATF PEP definition and Article R. 561-18 C. mon. fin. Ongoing risk-based screening is required after on-boarding; the CDD/AML file must be retained for five years after the end of the business relationship under Article L. 561-33 C. mon. fin.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (procedures.inpi.fr), with antecedent search performed through the Infogreffe portal (RCS database) and the INPI trademark database (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings must be in French under the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994). The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may include foreign words but must be written in the Latin script, be pronounceable and presented in a transliteration acceptable to French registry practice, and be clearly followed by the legal form 'SAS' and the registered office address. All non-French supporting documents submitted to the registry require a certified French translation (traduction assermentée).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a binding pre-registration name reservation; the 30-day window denotes the practical deadline to complete the Guichet Unique filing once availability has been confirmed. Upon rejection of the name by the Greffe/INPI through the Guichet Unique, the founder must (i) review the precise ground stated in the refusal notice (identity or patrimonial confusion with a prior RCS entry or prior trademark, or infringement of Article R. 123-38 of the Commercial Code); (ii) where a private prior right is asserted, obtain a written waiver or coexistence agreement (lettre de renonciation / accord de coexistence) from the prior right holder, or amend the name and resubmit the dossier; (iii) where the registrar's refusal is contested on legal grounds, file an application before the President of the Tribunal judiciaire (or the Tribunal de commerce for commercial disputes) of the place of the registered office by way of the simplified accelerated procedure, within 15 days of notification of the refusal decision, through a French avocat.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a French SAS under Article L. 123-11-1 of the Commercial Code through a formal domiciliation contract (contrat de domiciliation) with an authorized domiciliation company (société de domiciliation agréée). Virtual office use is acceptable for the low-risk B2B Enterprise SaaS activity (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210); however, the domiciliation address cannot substitute for genuine operational substance for tax residence purposes, and the place of effective management and decision-making must align with the siège social under Article 209 of the Code général des impôts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low annualized risk estimated at less than 5% in the first year post-incorporation. Unannounced on-site inspections by DGFiP are rare because tax audits (vérification de comptabilité) require prior written notification; unannounced visits are more plausible through a control de domiciliation conducted by the Greffe, Gendarmerie, or URSSAF where the registered office appears fictitious. A properly substantiated domiciliation contract and accessible management premises reduce the probability below 1% for a clean, license-exempt SaaS company.

UBO, PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and French Treasury sanctions screening compliance package
SAS registration through the Guichet Unique incl. RCS inscription fees (frais d'immatriculation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (official INPI and greffe fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the constitution notice (avis de constitution) in a legal gazette (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-determined rate per line or fixed statutory stock-company insert rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank attestation of share capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
12-month registered office domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approx. USD 55-85 per month)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SAS articles of association (statuts), corporate records and filing assistance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (flat or hourly fee under engagement letter)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign UBO and corporate documents (traduction assermentée)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff / certified translator rate schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles and consular legalization of foreign-issued documents (estimated 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign Apostille authorities and French consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular and administrative fees of the issuing state

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Miscellaneous administrative costs: SIRENE registration, initial CFE declaration, and corporate file consumables

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) — general company provisions L.210-1 et seq., SAS-specific provisions L.227-1 to L.227-30, and RCS registration provisions R.123-1 et seq.; implemented through the Guichet Unique under Décret n°2021-1628 and Loi n°2021-1729 du 22 décembre 2021.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), filing exclusively via the Guichet Unique electronic portal operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration unique de création d'entreprise (single incorporation declaration, form 11677*02 digitized) filed as 'Création d'une société — SAS', which simultaneously triggers RCS registration, INSEE SIREN/SIRET allocation, URSSAF affiliation and DGFiP tax identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS share capital is freely fixed in the articles; French law imposes no statutory minimum and no fixed escrow percentage. The full subscribed cash capital must nevertheless be credited to a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) at a credit institution and is released to the company only upon issuance of the Kbis registration certificate; in-kind contributions require a commissaire aux apports valuation unless a waiver applies, and contributions must be effectively made before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned founders of [Company], a société par actions simplifiée in formation, in first assembly, resolve: (1) Articles of Association in the submitted form, whose object covers enterprise software design, development, distribution and B2B SaaS services, are adopted; (2) the share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares, is subscribed and fully paid into the blocked account of [Bank], to be released upon delivery of the Kbis certificate; (3) the registered office is fixed at [address], France; (4) [Name] is appointed Président with broadest powers to bind the company, open bank accounts, and complete registration formalities; (5) the Président is instructed to exercise all necessary powers before the Guichet Unique and the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association and ancillary founder declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders with French legal counsel (Avocat); voluntary notarial certification if a contribution of real estate or continuing business is planned; no government window at this preparatory stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statutes containing corporate form, corporate name, proposed registered office, corporate object limited to ISIC 6201 activities (design, development, publishing and maintenance of enterprise software and B2B SaaS), share capital and share classes, governance powers of the Président, shareholders' decision rules, and dissenting and transmission clauses; have each founder sign every page and the signature page (qualified electronic signatures accepted); concurrently prepare the beneficial owner declaration schedule (RBE), the non-conviction declaration of the manager, and the office premises occupancy title.
required_dossiers: Articles of association (statuts) signed by all shareholders
Identification documents (passport or national ID) of each founder and the appointed Président
Declaration of non-conviction (déclaration de non-condamnation) of the Président
Beneficial owner declaration (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE) with supporting documents
Occupancy title or landlord consent for the registered office
Power of attorney if the filing is made through a proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any statutory defect identified by counsel or by the registry notification within the 15-day cure period; re-execute the affected pages with a fresh qualified signature; no additional registry fee applies for a single corrective act if the original declaration is merely completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital escrow account and deposit of the subscribed share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed credit institution in France or another EEA member state offering a compte bloqué (blocked company-formation account), which issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the proposed corporate name after completing enhanced KYC; transfer the full amount of the subscribed cash capital; obtain the bank certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) indicating the total deposits and the account reference; the depositary bank releases the funds automatically only against presentation of the Kbis extract, protecting creditors during formation.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Temporary account opening contract or account identification document
Identity documents of the founders as sole signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the selected bank declines the relationship, invoke the Banque de France droit au compte (right to an account) procedure or use any other licensed EU credit institution; obtain a fresh deposit certificate and re-present it to the Guichet Unique without reopening the whole file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the mandatory legal convention notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Newspaper authorized to publish legal announcements (Journal d'Annonces Légales — JAL) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place the avis de constitution containing the requisite RIP adjuncts: corporate form (SAS), registered name, corporate object, registered office, amount of share capital, duration, and identification of the legal manager; the gazette validates the wording and issues an attestation de parution, which must be appended to the Guichet Unique file; the registry is entitled to verify publicity within one month of filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal announcement (projet d'avis) signed by the legal representative
Attestation de parution issued by the gazette after publication
Proof of payment of the gazette fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requires corrections, adapt and republish the corrected notice; if publication timing conflicts with the registry deadline, request an attestation de parution anticipée from the gazette or await the official certificate — the Greffe normally offers a 30-working-day window for production of the publication evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the single incorporation declaration through the Guichet Unique to the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI, with pre-validation by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce of the registered office location and routing to URSSAF, INSEE and DGFiP.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In the portal, choose 'Création d'une société — SAS'; enter corporate particulars, registered office address, activity code 6201Z (Programmation informatique), manager information, shareholding structure including RBE data, and attach the signed statutes, capital deposit certificate, JAL publication attestation, founder identities, non-conviction declarations, premises occupancy title, and proof of fee payment; pay the registry fee online; monitor the status of the declaration and respond to any request from the registrar; a green file triggers simultaneous INSEE SIREN/SIRET, URSSAF employer account, DGFiP tax and VAT registration and social identification.
required_dossiers: Statutes signed by all founders (single PDF with page numbering and signatures)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the bank
Attestation de parution of the legal notice
Identity documents of all founders and the Président
Declaration of non-conviction and RBE declaration
Occupancy title or rental consent for the registered office
Proof of payment of registry fees and publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an adverse intervention query, supply the missing documents or rectified statutes within the statutory cure period, generally 15 calendar days, through the same portal; if registration is refused, petition the Président du Tribunal de commerce in chambers (référé); a refusal should be appealed jointly against the Greffe and the adjudicating authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of the Kbis extract and activation of automatic secondary registrations, tax and social identifiers, and data protection formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce delivering Kbis; INSEE allocating SIREN and SIRET; URSSAF receiving the employer declaration and DPAE; DGFiP issuing the intra-Community VAT number; CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés) for data-processing registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After final validation, retrieve the electronic Kbis (official RCS registration certificate) from the Greffe; confirm issuance of SIREN and SIRET codes and the TVA intracommunautaire number; register the company as employer before any payroll; file the mandatory processing of personal data register with the CNIL before putting the SaaS platform in production; keep the Kbis, articles and register of shareholders at the registered office for third-party verification so as to satisfy French transparency and Code de commerce record-keeping duties.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract and RCS permanent file
SIREN and SIRET numbers issued by INSEE
Intra-Community VAT number issued by DGFiP
URSSAF employer affiliation certificate
CNIL filing receipt (declaration normale or compliance evidence) where personal data are processed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed, obtain a provisional attestation de dépôt from the Greffe confirming filing; if INSEE or URSSAF identifiers are erroneous, request correction through the Guichet Unique update function; if CNIL rejects the declaration, segregate high-risk processing until the revised file is accepted; if registration is refused, initiate the référé procedure before the President of the competent Tribunal de commerce.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 (software programming) — a B2B SaaS venture is a fully liberal commercial and tertiary activity exempt from industrial authorization; the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) has only an optional innovation-support role; no préfecture or licensing board permit is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — the sole operating title is the RCS registration evidenced by the Kbis extract; no manufacturing, operating or premises-based industrial permit exists for enterprise software activities; supplementary filings with CNIL or AMF authorization apply only if sub-activities enter regulated sectors such as payment services or financial data processing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires — Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE), non-applicable to software offices
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required for the ISIC 6201 tertiary activity; software programming is absent from the listed project categories of Article R.122-2 of the Code de l'environnement, and no ICPE installation thresholds for waste, wastewater or emissions are met.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for wastewater, VOCs or hazardous substances — zero industrial discharge regime; administrative compliance is limited to e-waste disposal through licensed eco-organismes (e.g., ecosystem, Ecologic) under the AGEC law (anti-waste circular economy) and office sorting obligations set by the Code de l'environnement, Title IV.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office facilities must satisfy the Code du travail's workplace safety standards: written single risk assessment (DUERP), periodic electrical installation verification, workstation ergonomics, and registration of staff with the occupational health service (médecine du travail). Premises open to the public must meet the ERP fire-safety code: for standard office use under fifth-category thresholds, a simple compliance declaration suffices; the prior hiring declaration to URSSAF (DPAE) and, for any new building, the certificate of structural conformity complete occupational clearance. No major-risk (ICPE) evacuation plan is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official tax portal impots.gouv.fr. Business-registration data and the SIREN/SIRET identifiers are issued through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). Customs identifiers are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SAS and file formation formalities through the INPI Guichet unique. 2. Obtain the SIREN identifying the legal entity and the SIRET identifying each establishment from the competent registration system. 3. Open and activate the professional account on impots.gouv.fr and identify the competent SIE based on the registered establishment or French tax representative. 4. Register for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll taxes where applicable, and other relevant tax accounts through the SIE and required tax forms. 5. Obtain the French VAT identification number, generally formatted as FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN. 6. For a foreign entity without a French establishment, submit the VAT-registration application to the DGFiP foreign-business service, provide constitutional documents, tax-residence evidence, business contracts, expected French transactions, identity and authority documents, and appoint a French fiscal representative where required. Businesses established in another EU Member State are generally not required to appoint a French fiscal representative; non-EU businesses generally must appoint an approved French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exemption applies. 7. Obtain an EORI number from French customs before conducting customs operations in France or using France as the relevant customs Member State. 8. Maintain current registered-address, beneficial-owner, bank-account, VAT, and activity information and update the SIE and INPI systems when facts change.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. A qualifying SAS may make a temporary election for taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu), generally for a maximum of five financial years, if statutory conditions concerning size, age of the business, ownership, management, voting rights, and turnover or balance-sheet limits are satisfied. The election must be made within the statutory deadline and is subject to revocation and eligibility rules. France has no United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 apply to relevant cross-border arrangements; they do not provide a general elective hybrid-entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), consisting principally of French domestic VAT and EU VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold permits a French SAS conducting taxable business activities to remain outside VAT registration where VAT registration is otherwise required. The French franchise en base de TVA exemption for services generally applies below EUR 37,500 annual turnover, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250, subject to the applicable year-specific rules and activity classification. The corresponding principal threshold for goods is generally EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. A business using the franchise cannot recover input VAT and must monitor the applicable thresholds. VAT registration may nevertheless be required from the outset for intra-EU transactions, imports, exports, reverse-charge transactions, or an election to charge VAT. B2B SaaS supplies are generally governed by the customer-location rule and may be outside French VAT where supplied to a business customer established outside France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through accredited private platforms and the public invoicing infrastructure. From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices, and large and medium-sized businesses are scheduled to issue electronic invoices for domestic B2B transactions. Small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises are scheduled to issue such invoices from 1 September 2027. Electronic reporting applies to transactions outside the domestic B2B e-invoicing perimeter, including certain B2C and cross-border transactions, according to the statutory timetable. France does not generally operate a universal real-time VAT clearance requirement for every invoice. Required data must be transmitted in prescribed formats through an authorized platform, with invoice identity, supplier and customer identifiers, tax amounts, transaction classification, payment terms, and applicable cross-border or reverse-charge data. Digital archiving, invoice integrity, authenticity, readability, and audit-trail requirements apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT only where the exporter can establish that the goods left the EU customs territory and all export conditions are satisfied. The exporter must retain the customs export declaration, the electronic exit confirmation or equivalent customs proof, commercial invoices, transport evidence, and a consistent accounting trail. For B2B SaaS and other electronically supplied services, the principal rule is generally not a French zero rate but application of the place-of-supply rule: a service supplied to a business customer established outside France is normally taxable at the customer location, with the customer accounting for VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism where applicable. The supplier must verify and document the customer's business status, location, VAT number or equivalent tax evidence, contractual recipient, user and billing information, and the actual nature of the service. Supplies to EU business customers generally require reverse-charge invoicing and may trigger European Sales List reporting. French input VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, business-purpose evidence, proper VAT treatment, and timely VAT-return reporting. Export VAT refunds are subject to documentary verification and may be denied or reclaimed if export conditions are not proven.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the French exporter, customer, goods, value, currency, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Electronic export customs declaration, including the applicable customs procedure, commodity classification, customs value, and EORI identifiers
Movement Reference Number or equivalent customs reference
Customs exit confirmation, such as the electronic exit result or equivalent proof that the goods left the European Union
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier manifest, or other independent transport document
Packing list and proof of delivery where relevant
Sales contract, purchase order, customer correspondence, and accounting records linking the shipment to the invoice
Import or destination-country customs evidence where reasonably available
For B2B services, customer VAT or business-status evidence, contract, service-delivery records, customer location evidence, and reverse-charge invoice
Bank receipt or payment records where relevant; France does not generally require an inward-remittance certificate as a universal statutory condition for export VAT treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Exporters must nevertheless retain adequate commercial, customs, accounting, transport, customer-location, and payment records and comply with applicable anti-money-laundering, customs, and financial-reporting requirements. If zero-rating or non-taxation is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess French VAT, deny or claw back input-VAT credits or refunds, and charge late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Deliberate non-compliance may attract a 40% penalty; fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse may attract an 80% penalty, in addition to recovered VAT and interest. False customs declarations may result in customs duties, customs penalties, seizure, and potentially criminal liability. Fraudulent VAT refund claims, falsified export evidence, or knowingly incorrect customer-location or reverse-charge treatment may also result in criminal tax-fraud exposure and exclusion from simplified compliance or refund procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, with foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments oversight shared with the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, including the Directorate-General of the Treasury
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and operates within the European Union single market and the euro-area framework. Current-account payments, including customer receipts, supplier payments, payroll, service fees, royalties, dividends, interest, and ordinary profit remittances, are generally freely transferable without prior foreign-exchange approval. Capital-account movements are also generally liberalized, subject to anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, foreign-direct-investment screening, company-law, and beneficial-ownership requirements. An SAS may remit dividends or other distributions to non-resident shareholders only after legally distributable profits are established, annual accounts are approved, mandatory legal reserves and other restrictions are satisfied, withholding-tax treatment is determined, and the payment is supported by corporate resolutions and accounting records. Related-party loans, management charges, royalties, interest, and other cross-border payments must be commercially justified, arm's-length where applicable, properly documented, and reported or withheld where required. SaaS software development and ordinary enterprise software licensing generally do not fall within France's sensitive-sector foreign-direct-investment authorization regime, but the analysis must be repeated if the business handles sensitive technology, defense-related data, critical infrastructure, regulated health data, or other protected activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender or mandatorily convert export proceeds into euros, and there is no general mandatory conversion ratio or statutory repatriation deadline for ordinary software and SaaS export receipts. Proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency, subject to bank documentation, sanctions screening, accounting, tax, and applicable balance-of-payments reporting obligations. The SAS should retain customer contracts, invoices, delivery or acceptance evidence, bank statements, and foreign-currency accounting records. Any reporting requested by the Banque de France or a regulated financial institution must be completed within the applicable reporting period. Export controls, sanctions, VAT evidence, and transfer-pricing documentation remain separate from foreign-exchange convertibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS share subscriptions / Operational Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS share subscriptions / Operational Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne institutions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for payment collection, SEPA transfers, foreign-currency accounts, and treasury support where the provider is an EEA-authorized payment institution or electronic-money institution passported into France. Medium for use as the sole banking relationship because an EMI is not a credit institution, generally does not provide ordinary deposit protection, and must safeguard customer funds rather than accept deposits as a bank. Offshore providers outside the EEA cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to French customers merely by operating from abroad; they require an appropriate French or EEA authorization, passporting basis, or regulated correspondent arrangement. Wise Europe S.A. and similar EEA-regulated providers may be operationally suitable subject to onboarding, supported currencies, local account availability, transaction limits, safeguarding terms, and source-of-funds review. Stripe Billing is a payment-acceptance and merchant-services rail, not a substitute for a French corporate bank account. Maintain a domestic bank account for share-capital deposits, taxes, payroll, statutory payments, reserve liquidity, and contingency operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks may permit remote onboarding using qualified or bank-approved electronic identification, video verification, electronic signatures, and certified corporate documents. Physical attendance by directors is not a universal statutory requirement, but the bank may require a branch meeting, video interview, live identity verification, or in-person presentation of original documents based on risk, nationality, ownership complexity, foreign directors, unusual activity, or inability to validate the registered office. The legal representative, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and controlling persons must be identified and verified. A French registered office, valid company registration evidence, tax information, business rationale, expected transaction profile, and an accessible operating contact materially improve approval prospects.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ownership involving non-transparent holding companies, nominee shareholders, trusts, bearer instruments, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or equivalent registration record; articles of association; complete ownership chart to the natural-person beneficial owners; shareholder register; identification documents and proof of address for all beneficial owners and controllers; beneficial-owner declaration; board or shareholder resolutions; and certified translations where requested

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors or shareholders whose identity, residential address, tax residence, or authority cannot be independently verified
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or national identity document; recent proof of residential address; tax-identification information; director appointment evidence; notarized or bank-approved powers of attorney; video-identification availability; corporate registry extracts; and a written explanation of the cross-border ownership and management structure

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or large initial transfers inconsistent with the stated SaaS business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement; shareholder or board funding resolution; bank statements showing the originating account; audited or management financial statements of the funding entity; source-of-wealth evidence for relevant individuals; loan agreement where applicable; investment or financing agreement; transfer-pricing or intercompany rationale; and a transaction-by-transaction funds-flow schedule

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model described only as software or technology without verifiable customers, products, contracting entities, or expected payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product description; website and product demonstration; customer contracts or representative order forms; invoices; subscription pricing; projected monthly transaction volumes; countries of customers and suppliers; expected currencies; service-delivery model; data-processing arrangements; and explanation distinguishing software services from regulated financial, crypto-asset, gambling, or payment activity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity inconsistent with the stated low-risk B2B SaaS profile, including high-volume pass-through payments, cash activity, unrelated third-party funds, virtual-asset exposure, or payments from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved customer and supplier geography matrix; prohibited-country and sanctions screening procedure; transaction-monitoring rules; payment-flow diagram; customer due-diligence standards; documented prohibition on third-party funds and cash; projected account turnover; and escalation procedures for unusual transactions

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse media, export-control, or restricted-party screening hit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent identity verification; ownership and control analysis; written false-positive assessment; sanctions-screening results; adverse-media review; explanation of the person's role; contractual restrictions; export-control classification where relevant; and compliance-officer certification that no prohibited relationship or transaction exists

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office, tax-residence, or operational-substance concerns, including a mailbox address or no credible French business presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or domiciliation agreement; proof of operating premises; utility or service evidence where available; French registration and tax documents; employee or contractor information; management and development-location explanation; customer and supplier contracts; and a written rationale for any foreign headquarters, remote workforce, or outsourced development

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate documentation, inconsistent names or addresses, expired certificates, unsigned documents, or documents not in an accepted language
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recently issued registry extracts; legalized or apostilled documents where required; consistent English or French translations; certified copies; specimen signatures; current articles and resolutions; document-index checklist; and a single controlled corporate-data room

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment processors, offshore intermediaries, or fintech accounts used as the principal source or destination of funds without a clear regulated basis
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider authorization and regulatory-status evidence; account ownership confirmation; processor agreement; settlement-flow diagram; merchant-acquiring terms; reconciliation reports; customer funds segregation explanation; and justification for each payment intermediary

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route share subscriptions and shareholder funding through an account in the SAS's legal name at a French credit institution or an appropriately regulated EEA provider, with the transfer originating from the subscriber's or lender's own verified account. Use a clear payment reference identifying the SAS, the subscription or loan nature, and the relevant corporate resolution. For a new SAS, use the bank's blocked capital-deposit account until the share capital is validly formed and the deposit certificate is issued; subsequently transfer funds to the operational account after registration and completion of the bank's release process. Provide the bank with the subscription agreement, articles, capital table, corporate resolutions, beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds evidence, and originating bank details. For non-euro funds, confirm conversion rates, intermediary-bank charges, value date, and whether the recipient account accepts the currency. There is no single universal French purpose-code system for ordinary corporate capital transfers; the bank may require an internal transaction purpose, ISO payment message information, loan or equity classification, and supporting documents. Avoid unexplained third-party funding, informal netting, cash delivery, or transfers through personal accounts. Reconcile the incoming transfer to the general ledger and retain the complete audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT cross-border credit transfers, typically ISO 20022 pacs.008 in modern bank channels and legacy MT103 where still supported, for non-SEPA or non-euro supplier payments. Include accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, ultimate-debtor, invoice, purpose, and sanctions-screening data; select OUR, SHA, or BEN charge allocation according to the contract and bank capability. For material or higher-risk purchases, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee. A commercial LC should specify issuing and confirming banks, applicable UCP 600 rules, required documents, Incoterms, shipment or service milestones, presentation period, currency, expiry, discrepancy handling, and sanctions and export-control conditions. For SaaS services, ordinary wire or SEPA settlement is generally more practical than an LC, but an LC may be relevant for hardware, implementation, cloud infrastructure, or cross-border procurement with documentary performance conditions. Maintain purchase orders, supplier invoices, contracts, acceptance evidence, VAT treatment, customs records for any hardware, and payment approvals. Apply dual authorization, beneficiary-change callback controls, transaction limits, and reconciliation to accounts payable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm for forecast or committed foreign-currency receipts and payments, subject to appropriate purpose, tenor, limits, collateral, and documentation

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies where physical delivery is restricted or commercially impractical, subject to counterparty availability, local-market rules, EMIR and MiFID-related obligations, and documented hedging purpose

Cross-currency swaps and currency swaps for longer-dated financing or recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral terms, valuation, accounting designation, and counterparty-credit approval
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-date management

Currency options, collars, and other structured hedges where proportionate to the exposure and approved under the treasury policy; avoid leveraged or speculative structures unless separately authorized
Euro-denominated SEPA settlement and natural hedging by matching foreign-currency receipts with foreign-currency supplier costs, where commercially and operationally feasible

All derivatives should be entered into with regulated counterparties, documented under an appropriate master agreement, linked to identifiable exposures, monitored for counterparty and market risk, and recorded under applicable French GAAP or IFRS hedge-accounting policies; speculative dealing should be prohibited by the treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting approval of annual accounts (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory minute book; no government filing at approval stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year end; extension only by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting prevents lawful annual accounts filing; court injunction possible; corporate officers may incur civil liability; no administrative strike-off at this stage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing at the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (electronic filing via Infogreffe / formalités entreprise)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after fiscal year end; for calendar-year-end SAS, by 31 July; if accounts approved before the six-month point, filing is due within one month after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing can trigger court injunction with daily fines and court-imposed penalties up to EUR 1,500 for legal entities; repeated non-deposit after formal notice enables the public prosecutor to request administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax result declaration (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), electronic filing service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year-end: e-filing by 18 May of the following year; non-calendar fiscal year: e-filing by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% late-filing penalty plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; deliberate non-filing may increase penalties to 40% and add criminal fines; tax authority may assess estimated taxable income and initiate enforced recovery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration update following shareholding changes (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within fifteen days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; no annual filing is required if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false UBO declarations expose the company to anti-money-laundering fines and registry penalties; repeated failure to maintain current UBO data may support court sanctions, but administrative strike-off is not the direct consequence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is required if the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the close of the fiscal year: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average staff above 50 employees. A statutory auditor is also required for companies that control or are controlled by entities meeting these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles as codified in the Plan Comptable Général and règlement ANC n° 2014-03 apply to statutory individual financial statements. IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts of groups; a standalone SAS must prepare its legal accounts under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation statement. The SAS must maintain a current register of beneficial owners on site and deliver an updated UBO declaration to the Greffe within fifteen days after any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership. At the annual ordinary general meeting, the president should review the shareholder register and confirm that the UBO register reflects any shareholding movements, recording such verification in the minutes.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Professional domiciliation office: EUR 300–800 per year (approx USD 320–870). Full corporate secretarial agent with registered office services: EUR 1,500–4,500 per year (approx USD 1,600–4,850).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Mandatory statutory audit for a mid-sized SAS: EUR 4,000–12,000 per year (approx USD 4,300–13,000). If the SAS is below statutory audit thresholds, no audit fee is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year end (e.g. 15 April for FY ending 31 Dec)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for qualifying EU parent-subsidiary; 25% statutory rate otherwise, reduced by bilateral tax treaties (e.g. 5% US, 10% UK)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC application on impots.gouv.fr with supporting documents including ownership proof, beneficial ownership, and treaty eligibility criteria
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory, 0-10% under treaties (e.g. 0% US-FTAs); Interest: 25% statutory, 0% under EU IARD for intra-group loans meeting conditions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million for Local File; €750 million consolidated revenue for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces Economic Substance via DAC6 reporting and specific substance requirements for IP holding companies and certain service providers; must demonstrate real economic activity in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent understatement of income or false invoicing to reduce tax base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanction: up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to 80% of the evaded tax; civil recovery of taxes plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for fines and imprisonment; possible disqualification and ban on directorships

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's length transactions without economic substance or failing to maintain TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to €10 million or 5% of annual turnover; tax reassessment with penalties and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal administrative fines and potential criminal liability if intent to evade

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cross-border payments to avoid or underpay WHT or mischaracterizing as non-taxable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WHT evasion penalty up to 80% of tax due; possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, and in extreme cases imprisonment; travel restrictions possible
